faq.q: How many homes can I have on an ALR acreage?
faq.a: Generally one principal residence (maximum 500 m² total floor area), plus, where the property qualifies, one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha; more than that, or a larger residence, requires ALC approval, and local bylaws may restrict further.

faq.q: Can I stratify or subdivide an ALR acreage into strata lots?
faq.a: Not without the ALC's permission: depositing a strata plan is a subdivision, and ALCA s. 21(1) bars subdividing agricultural land unless the Commission permits it or the ALR General Regulation allows it (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6).

faq.q: What farm income does an acreage need to keep farm classification?
faq.a: BC Assessment's minimum gross farm income (farm gate) thresholds are $2,500 for an operation of 0.8 ha to 4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation, and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha; new applications are due by the legislated October 31 deadline.

faq.q: Which communities does this page's feed cover?
faq.a: At reading, the visible cards were labelled with Langley sub-areas (County Line Glen Valley, Willoughby Heights, Campbell Valley, Salmon River, Otter District) and Abbotsford sub-areas (Abbotsford West, Poplar), at $1,699,000–$5,995,000 in card text — a regional feed, which is why no single community's statistics are presented as this page's figures.
